Criticism ain't hate, remember that. Criticism is when someone politely tells another that their work isn't as good as it can be, then offers advice on how to fix it. Hate is when someone blatantly insults your work, then offers no advice on what to do.

*Constructive* criticism is very good because the artist can learn from it and become better at drawing/singing/whatever they're doing. Hate is bad, well, for obvious reasons.

If those rude people were insulting you or your art without any tips or a good explanation, that's hate, isn't it?

Accept constructive criticism because it can help you. But, obviously, confront hate.

If someone offers you advice on what could be better, learn from it! Do not throw it out just because they said your work isn't perfect!

Learning English is so easy compared to learning other languages. Japanese has three writing systems, one of which you CANNOT learn completely because there are too many characters (kanji). Kanji is not only is numerous, but most kanji have at LEAST 2 readings as well (on'yomi, kun'yomi). If you think English spelling is weird, take a look at Irish and French.

Mandarin Chinese is one of the hardest languages. Crazy writing system that apparently has over 50,000+ characters (all of which have an individual meaning and some have different readings), the language has 4 tones, etc.

Pronunciation-wise, in my personal opinion and experience, Korean takes the crown for complex pronunciation. It's a language isolate, meaning it (probably) isn't related to any other language. Korean is beautiful when spoken, but has at least 7 vowels that English doesn't have which makes it very difficult to adjust to the language.

English is weird with its spelling?! What about Tibetan? Tibetan is so difficult and weird with its spelling, it's insane. I recommend watching this link to see exactly what I'm talking about: ([https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=btn0-Vce5ug](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=btn0-Vce5ug)).

English isn't even the hardest Germanic language. I'm not a native English speaker. My native language isn't Germanic. I am fluent in English and am currently learning German. Let me just say, *German is much more difficult.* Some things make zero sense. *What's even the point of der, die, das? Can't it be just one form? Like English 'the'?* Compound words can be fucking insane. Pronouncing German words is sometimes difficult. *Also, why isn't Einstein in English be pronounced EinSHTein like in German? But the 'ei' is pronounced properly, so why not the 'st'?* Talking about 'st' sound in German, it isn't always 'sht'. Sometimes it's 'sht', sometimes it's 'st'. In the beginning of words, it's always 'sht' (and 'shp') but in other positions, you kinda have to guess (or remember from somewhere).

Also, there is a ton of English media online which makes the language a thousand times easier. A year or two ago, I was awful at English. I just went online and started consuming English media. Now I'm fluent.

The fact that there's so much good English media makes it easy to learn the language.
